source.gazette: The Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II - Section 3(i), No. 124, dated 9 March 2011
source.note: Base 2011 text + amendments applied and dated inline as GSR 784(E) processed so far. Remaining amendments (2012-2026) to be layered as they are processed - each carries its own effective_from date.

commencement_date_correction.note: GSR 779(E) (02.11.2021) originally set its own commencement (via principal Rule 1(2)) as 01.04.2022. GSR 226(E) SUBSTITUTED that date to 01.10.2022 - so all GSR 779(E) changes took legal effect on 01.10.2022, not 01.04.2022 as originally notified. All effective_from dates in this JSON that trace to GSR 779(E) have been corrected to 2022-10-01 accordingly. FURTHER PUSHED by GSR 747(E), 30.09.2022: GSR 226(E)'s own commencement date (which it had set as 01.10.2022) was itself substituted again to 01.12.2022. So the FINAL, current effective date for all GSR 226(E) changes (Rule 6(11) resubstitution, Rule 33(2) omission, Second Schedule omission) AND all GSR 779(E) changes that GSR 226(E) had already re-dated, is 01.12.2022 - not 01.10.2022. All such dates in this JSON have been corrected accordingly. FURTHER PUSHED AGAIN by GSR 859(E), 30.11.2022: GSR 226(E)'s commencement date (which GSR 747(E) had already moved to 01.12.2022) was substituted once more, to 01.01.2023. So the FINAL, current effective date for all GSR 226(E) changes (and the GSR 779(E) changes GSR 226(E) had re-dated) is 01.01.2023, not 01.12.2022. Note this now coincides with GSR 648(E)'s own effective date (Rule 26(f) loose garment exemption), also 01.01.2023 - both landed on the same commencement date. FURTHER PUSHED (4th and 5th time) by GSR 910(E), dated 29.12.2022 (NOT YET SEEN/PROCESSED - see known_gaps GAP_3) and then GSR 60(E), dated 27.01.2023: the commencement date progressed 01.01.2023 -> 01.02.2023 (per GSR 910(E), inferred) -> 01.04.2023 (per GSR 60(E), confirmed). FINAL current effective date for the GSR 226(E)/779(E) chain is now 01.04.2023. This does NOT affect GSR 648(E)'s Rule 26(f) garment exemption, which remains its own separate notification effective 01.01.2023. FURTHER PUSHED (6th time) by GSR 214(E), dated 24.03.2023: commencement date moved from 01.04.2023 to 01.06.2023. FINAL current effective date for the GSR 226(E)/779(E) chain is now 01.06.2023. GSR 648(E)'s separate Rule 26(f) garment exemption remains unaffected (01.01.2023). FURTHER PUSHED (7th time) by GSR 412(E), dated 05.06.2023: commencement date moved from 01.06.2023 to 01.07.2023. Current effective date for the GSR 226(E)/779(E) chain is now 01.07.2023 - still subject to further pushes if more amendments in this chain are found. FURTHER PUSHED (8th time) by GSR 463(E), dated 28.06.2023: commencement date moved from 01.07.2023 to 01.09.2023. Current effective date for the GSR 226(E)/779(E) chain is now 01.09.2023. FURTHER PUSHED (9th time) by GSR 640(E), dated 30.08.2023: commencement date moved from 01.09.2023 to 01.10.2023. Current effective date for the GSR 226(E)/779(E) chain is now 01.10.2023. FURTHER PUSHED (10th time) by GSR 714(E), dated 30.09.2023: commencement date moved from 01.10.2023 to 01.01.2024 (a bigger jump than prior monthly pushes). Current effective date for the GSR 226(E)/779(E) chain is now 01.01.2024.
commencement_date_correction.prosecution_moratorium: GSR 226(E) clause 6 also provides: no prosecution shall be initiated against manufacturers/packers/importers who made declarations in accordance with GSR 779(E) rules starting from the ORIGINAL 01.04.2022 date - i.e., early/good-faith compliance during Apr-Sep 2022 is protected, not penalized, despite the date push-back

terms.consumer: INSERTED by GSR 629(E), 23.06.2017 as Rule 2(aa): same meaning as clause (d) of sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986. AMENDED by GSR 779(E), 02.11.2021, effective 01.04.2022: reference updated to clause (7) of section 2 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (the 1986 Act was repealed and replaced)
terms.e_commerce: INSERTED by GSR 629(E), 23.06.2017 as Rule 2(bd): buying and selling of goods and services, including digital products, over digital and electronic network
terms.e_commerce_entity: INSERTED by GSR 629(E), 23.06.2017 as Rule 2(be): a company incorporated under the Companies Act 1956/2013, or a foreign company/office/branch/agency in India (per FEMA 1999) owned/controlled by a person resident outside India, conducting e-commerce business
terms.marketplace_based_model_of_ecommerce: INSERTED by GSR 629(E), 23.06.2017 as Rule 2(bf): an IT platform provided by an e-commerce entity on a digital/electronic network to act as facilitator between buyer and seller
terms.dealer: Person/firm carrying on business of buying, selling, supplying or distributing packaged commodity (cash, deferred payment, or commission); includes commission agents; EXCLUDES manufacturers (unless manufacturer sells to a non-dealer)
terms.industrial_consumer: SUBSTITUTED by GSR 385(E), 14.05.2015 (originally inserted by GSR 359(E), 06.06.2013): consumer who buys packaged commodities directly from the manufacturer OR from an importer OR from a wholesale dealer, for use by that industry - AND the package MUST carry the declaration 'not for retail sale'. CHANGE: broadened sourcing beyond just manufacturer; NEW requirement of 'not for retail sale' label on the package itself
terms.institutional_consumer: SUBSTITUTED by GSR 629(E), 23.06.2017 (Rule 2(bc)): institution which buys packaged commodities BEARING A DECLARATION 'not for retail sale', directly from manufacturer/importer/wholesale dealer, for use by that institution AND NOT for commercial or trade purposes. CHANGE from 385(E) version: adds explicit requirement that the package itself must bear the 'not for retail sale' declaration, and adds 'not for commercial or trade purposes' restriction (tightens the definition to prevent institutional-exemption misuse for resale)
terms.lot: (i) For stored packages: total number stored; (ii) For packages on/at end of packing line: maximum hourly output
terms.manufacturer: Person/firm who produces/makes/manufactures the commodity; includes anyone who marks a package claiming it as their own product even if not actually made by them
terms.maximum_permissible_error: Error in deficiency in quantity of an individual package, per limits in First Schedule
terms.net_quantity: Quantity by weight/measure/number of commodity in a package, EXCLUDING packaging/wrappers
terms.packer: Person/firm who pre-packs any commodity into units suitable for wholesale or retail sale
terms.principal_display_panel: Total surface area of package where required info is given - either (i) all info grouped at one place, or (ii) pre-printed info grouped at one place + online/variable info grouped at another NEW PROVISO inserted by GSR 778(E), 23.10.2025: for packages containing MEDICAL DEVICES, the Medical Devices Rules 2017 apply instead to make declarations - LM(PC) Rules' PDP definition does not govern medical device packaging.
terms.retail_dealer: Dealer who sells directly to consumer; includes a wholesale dealer making a direct sale to consumer
terms.retail_package: Package intended for retail sale to ultimate consumer for consumption; includes imported packages. ORIGINAL proviso ('ultimate consumer excludes industrial/institutional consumers') OMITTED by GSR 359(E), 06.06.2013 - structural cleanup, substance unchanged. NEW proviso INSERTED by GSR 385(E), 14.05.2015: for 'retail food package', the definition under Food Safety and Standards Act 2006 rules/regulations applies instead
terms.retail_sale_price_MRP: SUBSTITUTED by GSR 629(E), 23.06.2017 (Rule 2(m)): maximum price at which the commodity in packaged form may be sold to the CONSUMER, inclusive of all taxes. CHANGE: simplified definition (dropped 'ultimate' consumer wording and the detailed printed-format/rounding text from the definition itself - printed format is now separately governed by Rule 6(1)(e), see R6_1_e)
terms.standard_package: A package containing the specified quantity of a commodity (i.e., matches Second Schedule quantities where applicable)
terms.wholesale_dealer: Dealer who does NOT sell directly to consumer, but distributes/sells via intermediaries
terms.wholesale_package: Package containing: (i) multiple retail packages not intended for direct single-consumer sale, or (ii) bulk commodity sold to an intermediary, or (iii) 10+ retail packages (provided each retail package is individually labeled as required)
terms.combination_package: INSERTED by GSR 722(E), 06.10.2023, effective 01.01.2024, as Rule 2(ka): a retail package containing 2+ individual packages/pieces of DISSIMILAR commodities (e.g., a set of spoons+knives+forks+cups+napkins)
terms.group_package: INSERTED by GSR 722(E), 06.10.2023, effective 01.01.2024, as Rule 2(kb): a retail package containing 2+ individual packages/pieces of SIMILAR BUT NOT IDENTICAL commodities (differ in weight/measure/volume/appearance/quality). Examples: assorted-size sponges in one pack, assorted biscuits, similar commodities of different brands packed together
terms.multi_piece_package: INSERTED by GSR 722(E), 06.10.2023, effective 01.01.2024, as Rule 2(kc): a package containing 2+ individually packaged/labelled pieces of the SAME commodity, IDENTICAL quantity each (e.g., 5 toilet soap cakes of 20g each, total 100g). For food articles, FSS Act 2006 applies instead of this definition.

additional_checks_from_general_provision.title: MRP tampering prohibition
additional_checks_from_general_provision.requirement: No dealer may obliterate, smudge or alter the retail sale price indicated by manufacturer/packer/importer. Manufacturer/packer/importer shall not alter the price on the wrapper once printed and used for packing.
additional_checks_from_general_provision.checklist_relevance: Directly checkable via image analysis - detect signs of MRP alteration/tampering/overwriting on scanned labels

additional_checks_from_general_provision.title: Advertisement declarations
additional_checks_from_general_provision.requirement: Any advertisement mentioning the retail sale price of a pre-packaged commodity must also contain a declaration of net quantity/number of the commodity
additional_checks_from_general_provision.font_rule: Font size of the net quantity declaration in the advertisement must match the font size of the retail sale price
additional_checks_from_general_provision.checklist_relevance: Relevant to your e-commerce/product-listing scanning feature - MRP in an online listing must be accompanied by net quantity in matching font size

additional_checks_from_general_provision.title: Fine for contravention
additional_checks_from_general_provision.requirement: Whoever contravenes any provision of these rules, for which no punishment is otherwise provided, shall be punished with a fine of Rs. 5,000. Rule 32A adds a compounding-of-offences table (same amounts as the GSR 359(E) table processed earlier - Rs.2000-50000 range depending on offence and applicant type).
additional_checks_from_general_provision.bucket: B - penalty/enforcement, not checklist-relevant, logged for completeness only
B - procedural (related to compounding of offences/court decisions), not checklist-relevant, logged for completeness only

additional_checks_from_general_provision.title: Electronics QR-Code Declaration Rule (NOW PERMANENT - was originally a 1-year pilot)
additional_checks_from_general_provision.applicability_window: REMOVED - no longer time-limited or restricted to products made after a specific date. Applies to ALL electronic products, ongoing, from 23.06.2023 onward.
additional_checks_from_general_provision.status: PERMANENT/CURRENT LAW as of GSR 456(E), 23.06.2023. The original GSR 577(E) pilot (14.07.2022) applied only to electronics manufactured/packed/imported after 15 July 2022, for ONE YEAR (window closed ~mid-2023). GSR 456(E) SUBSTITUTED the same provisos WITHOUT any date restriction - converting what was a temporary pilot into a STANDING, PERMANENT rule for all electronic products, effective immediately (date of publication, 23.06.2023).
additional_checks_from_general_provision.checklist_relevance: DIRECTLY ACTIONABLE for Category 4 (Electronics/Hardware) - unlike the earlier expired pilot, this is now standing law. For electronic products, a missing printed address/common-name/dimensions is NOT automatically a violation if a QR code is present and provides that info, AND the package tells the consumer to scan for it. Manufacturer name, phone, and email must still always be printed directly, never QR-only.

current_provisions.requirement: Package must print the manufacturer/packer/importer NAME on the package itself; ADDRESS and other related info MAY be deferred to a QR code, with an on-package note telling the consumer to scan for that info
Package may defer the common/generic name (and for multi-product packs, name+quantity of each product) to a QR code, with an on-package note directing the consumer to scan
Package may defer size/dimension info to a QR code, with an on-package note directing the consumer to scan
Phone number AND email address must remain printed ON the package itself (NOT QR-deferrable); only 'other related information' (e.g., full address) may be deferred to QR, with an on-package note

additional_checks_from_general_provision.requirement: Unit of quantity for this specific numbered commodity changed to: 'weight or volume, and if net quantity is declared by volume, it shall also be declared by weight' - same dual-declaration pattern as the Second Schedule edible oil rule
additional_checks_from_general_provision.bucket: B - Fourth Schedule data table entry, low priority, logged for completeness only (we don't have the full Fourth Schedule content since it was scoped out as Bucket B earlier)

additional_checks_from_general_provision.requirement: Rule 33's general power-to-relax-rules provision does NOT apply where the Medical Devices Rules 2017 are applicable - i.e., medical devices cannot seek relaxation under LM(PC) Rule 33 since they are already governed by MDR 2017 instead
additional_checks_from_general_provision.bucket: B - procedural/relaxation-power provision, but logged because it reinforces the medical-device-out-of-scope confirmation alongside Rule 2(h) and Rule 7(2)-(3) carve-outs

additional_checks_from_general_provision.requirement: Manufacturer registration procedure updates: (d) registration application must now include the name of the company Director responsible for violations; annual online update requirement for registered companies (address, products+quantities manufactured/packed/imported in the previous year, country of origin); registration certificates now remain valid until cancelled (no fixed expiry).
additional_checks_from_general_provision.bucket: B - manufacturer registration/administrative procedure, not label/declaration content - logged for completeness only, consistent with our established triage of Rule 27 as procedural

chapter_applicability.title: Application of Chapter (renamed from 'Applicability of the Chapter')
chapter_applicability.amendment_note: Rule 3 ENTIRELY SUBSTITUTED by GSR 629(E), 23.06.2017, effective 01.01.2018. This is now the CURRENT text, superseding the earlier version.
chapter_applicability.note: This is the MASTER exemption - if a package falls under (a), (b) or (c) below, the ENTIRE Chapter II (Rules 3-23, including all your checklist rules 6-17, 26) does not apply, not just individual declarations

excluded_from_chapter.text: Packages of commodities containing quantity MORE THAN 25 kg or 25 litre
excluded_from_chapter.amendment_note: CHANGE by GSR 629(E): the cement/fertilizer carve-out that used to be an exception WITHIN this clause has been moved out into its own separate clause (b) below, and broadened

excluded_from_chapter.text: Cement, fertilizer, AND agricultural farm produce sold in bags ABOVE 50 kilogram
excluded_from_chapter.amendment_note: NEW/BROADENED by GSR 629(E), 23.06.2017: 'agricultural farm produce' explicitly added to this >50kg exclusion basket alongside cement and fertilizer (previously agricultural produce >50kg was covered under old Rule 26(d) exemption, which is now OMITTED - see R26_d - since this Rule 3(b) covers it instead)

departmental_clarification.source: Departmental letter I-10/9/2023-W&M, dated 06.03.2023, Legal Metrology Division
departmental_clarification.clarification: Confirms the >50kg threshold is exact: packages of agricultural farm produce UP TO AND INCLUDING 50 kg are FULLY COVERED by Chapter II (not exempt) - only packages ABOVE 50kg are exempt. Manufacturers/packers/importers of farm produce are permitted to pack in ANY quantity up to 50kg (no fixed/standard quantity is mandated within that range for farm produce specifically) - but full Rule 6 declarations still apply since these packages ARE covered by the chapter.
departmental_clarification.checklist_relevance: For Category 1 farm produce specifically: do NOT flag varying/non-standard pack sizes up to 50kg as a violation - any quantity up to 50kg is legally permitted; but DO still check for full Rule 6 declarations (unlike genuinely exempt >50kg packages)

excluded_from_chapter.text: Packaged commodities meant for industrial consumers or institutional consumers
excluded_from_chapter.institutional_consumer_definition: See definitions.institutional_consumer (Rule 2(bc)) - as most recently substituted by GSR 629(E), now requires 'not for retail sale' declaration on the package + 'not for commercial/trade purposes' restriction
excluded_from_chapter.amendment_note: Substantive exemption unchanged from earlier (b) clause, just relettered to (c) since new (b) now covers cement/fertilizer/farm-produce

chapter_applicability.checklist_relevance: This confirms and legally grounds the 'Institutional/Industrial', '>25kg bulk', and 'agricultural produce >50kg' exemption pre-checks discussed for your architecture - these should run BEFORE any category checklist, since they exempt the whole chapter, not just one field

exemptions.condition: Net weight or measure of commodity is 10g or 10ml or less (if sold by weight/measure)
exemptions.note: ORIGINAL 2011 proviso (MRP+net qty still required for 10g-20g/10ml-20ml packages) REMOVED by GSR 784(E) dated 24.10.2011. NEW proviso INSERTED by GSR 385(E), 14.05.2015, effective 01.01.2016: this exemption (26(a)) does NOT apply to tobacco and tobacco products - such products must carry full declarations regardless of package size

tobacco_carveout.text: Provisions of this clause shall not be applicable for tobacco and tobacco products

pan_masala_carveout.text: Second further proviso: the <=10g/10ml exemption under Rule 26(a) shall NOT apply to pan masala - same treatment as the earlier tobacco carve-out (GSR 385(E), 2015). Pan masala packages must carry full declarations regardless of size.

exemptions.condition: Package containing fast food items packed by restaurant or hotel and the like
Contains scheduled formulations and non-scheduled formulations covered under the Drugs (Price Control) Order, 2013 (made under Essential Commodities Act 1955)
exemptions.amendment_note: SUBSTITUTED by GSR 629(E), 23.06.2017, effective 01.01.2018. CHANGE: reference updated from Drugs (Price Control) Order 1995 to the 2013 Order
exemptions.important_carveout: NEW proviso inserted by GSR 629(E): 'no exemption shall be applicable to medical devices declared as drugs' - i.e., medical devices do NOT get this drug exemption even if legally classified as drugs; they still need full LM(PC) declarations (subject also to the separate 2023 medical devices carve-out discussed elsewhere - see notes for that document if processed)
exemptions.departmental_confirmation: CONFIRMED by departmental letter I-10/17/2023-W&M, dated 10.07.2023: reiterates that medical devices declared as drugs are NOT exempt under Rule 26(c), and must comply with full LM(PC) declarations regardless of their drug classification.

exemptions.condition_historical: Previously: Agricultural farm produce in packages above 50 kg
exemptions.amendment_note: This exemption clause is REMOVED because agricultural farm produce >50kg is now covered by the broader Rule 3(b) chapter-inapplicability clause instead (see chapter_applicability.excluded_from_chapter R3_b) - substance preserved, just relocated to a stronger exclusion (whole-chapter inapplicability rather than a single-rule exemption)

exemptions.condition: Any thread sold in coil to handloom weavers
Garment or hosiery sold loose/open at point of sale, in a manner that lets the consumer inspect the product before buying - AND is a finished product
exemptions.note: This is a CONDITIONAL exemption - not a full exemption from all declarations. See quantity_declaration_rules.R26_f_and_garment_labeling for the reduced 4-field checklist that still applies (name/address, consumer care email+phone, size, MRP), plus the e-commerce display requirement if sold online.

exemptions.condition: Loose commodities ordered through e-commerce channels, where the consumer is already aware of the ordered commodity, its type, and quantity (i.e., not a physically pre-packaged product, but a loose item sold online where the listing itself informed the consumer)
exemptions.note: This is a NEW, BROADER exemption than Rule 26(f) - Rule 26(f) is specific to garments/hosiery sold loose in physical stores; Rule 26(g) covers ANY loose commodity (not just garments) ordered via e-commerce, provided the consumer already knew what they were ordering. Like 26(f), it is a CONDITIONAL exemption, not a full one - subject to a reduced declaration set.

required_fields.requirement: Of manufacturer, OR marketer, OR brand owner, OR importer, OR SELLER (broader list than Rule 26(f) - includes 'seller' too) + country of origin/manufacture if imported
Retail sale price inclusive of all taxes, in Indian currency
In standard unit of weight/measure, OR if sold by number, the count of the commodity

exemptions.checklist_relevance: DIRECTLY relevant to your e-commerce/listing-scanning feature for Category 1/4 (and beyond) - loose items sold online (e.g., bulk grains, loose produce, unpackaged hardware items sold by count) get this reduced 4-field checklist instead of full Rule 6, PROVIDED the e-commerce listing itself already conveyed commodity type+quantity to the consumer before purchase

declarations.requirement: Name and address of manufacturer; if manufacturer is not packer, name+address of both manufacturer and packer; for imported packages, name+address of importer
declarations.exception: Explanation III SUBSTITUTED by GSR 629(E), 23.06.2017, effective 01.01.2018: for food articles, this clause (a) does NOT apply at all - instead the Food Safety and Standards Act 2006 and rules made thereunder fully govern. CHANGE from earlier wording: strengthened from 'FSS Act applies instead' to an explicit full carve-out ('provisions of this clause shall not apply')

declarations.requirement: For imported products, the name of the country of origin, manufacture, or assembly shall be mentioned on the package
declarations.category_relevance: NEW mandatory field for all 3 categories (1/3/4) where the product is imported - directly checkable via OCR text search for a country name near origin/mfg declarations

declarations.requirement: Common or generic name of the commodity; if package has more than one product, name and number/quantity of each product
Net quantity in standard unit of weight/measure, or number if sold by count

Month and year commodity was manufactured. CHANGE by GSR 779(E), 02.11.2021, effective 01.04.2022: the words 'or pre-packed or imported' were OMITTED from this clause - meaning the declaration is now specifically the month/year of MANUFACTURE only, not alternatively pre-pack or import date. (Note: import-date-equivalent info is separately covered by the new Country of Origin field R6_1_aa)
exceptions: Proviso 1 - Food articles: Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 applies instead - UPDATED: originally Prevention of Food Adulteration Act 1954, substituted by GSR 427(E) dated 05.06.2012
Proviso 2 - Seeds labeled/certified under Seeds Act 1966 - exempt

Proviso 3 - REMOVED effective 01.07.2012 by GSR 784(E) (corrected by corrigendum GSR 832(E), 23.11.2011): originally allowed 'manufacturer may indicate month/year using a rubber stamp without overwriting' - this allowance no longer exists in current law
Proviso 4 - Cosmetics: Drugs and Cosmetics Rules 1945 applies instead
Not required on bidi or incense stick packages
Not required on domestic LPG cylinders (14.2kg or 5kg) marketed by public sector undertaking

Proviso 4th (added after the 'third proviso') - INSERTED by GSR 722(E), 06.10.2023, effective 01.04.2024: month/year of manufacture declaration does NOT apply to spare parts and accessories used for warranty servicing that are NOT sold to end customers

Proviso 5th - INSERTED by GSR 722(E), 06.10.2023, effective 01.04.2024: for electronic products' spare parts/accessories (that ARE sold to end customers), the month/year of manufacture must be specified ANYWHERE on the retail package, in a visible and clearly legible manner - i.e., no fixed PDP-grouping requirement for this specific field on such products
declarations.spare_parts_definition: Per Explanation inserted by GSR 722(E): 'spare parts and accessories' includes any part, component, or accessory complementary to the main/core product of a machine/device/equipment, including parts sold separately as replacements for damaged/worn-out parts

declarations.requirement: If a package contains a commodity which may become unfit for human consumption after a period of time, the 'best before or use by the date, month and year' shall be mentioned on the label
declarations.proviso: Does not apply if a provision on this is already made under any other law (e.g., FSS Act for food)

definitions.best_before: The date signifying the end of the period, under stated storage conditions, during which the product remains fully marketable and retains claimed qualities; beyond this date the commodity MAY still be safe for consumption
definitions.use_by_date: The date signifying the end of the estimated period, under stated storage conditions, after which the product no longer has the quality attributes normally expected; after this date the commodity should NOT be regarded as marketable

declarations.category_relevance: Category 1 (Food) primarily - directly checkable: flag if ONLY 'Best Before' appears with no 'Use By/Expiry' where the commodity is perishable

declarations.requirement: Retail sale price of the package

format_history.gsr_629E_2017: INSERTED illustrations (effective 01.01.2018): must clearly indicate it is the maximum retail price INCLUSIVE OF ALL TAXES, price rounded to nearest rupee or 50 paise. Acceptable formats illustrated: (a) 'Maximum or Max. retail price Rs./₹ xx.xx (inclusive of all taxes)', (b) 'Maximum or Max. retail price Rs./₹ xx.xx inclusive of all taxes', (c) 'MRP Rs./₹ xx.xx incl. of all taxes', (d) 'MRP Rs./₹ xx.xx (incl. of all taxes)'
format_history.gsr_779E_2021: SIMPLIFIED effective 01.04.2022: the detailed illustrated wording above was REPLACED with a single simpler requirement - the price must simply be stated 'in Indian currency'. CURRENT LAW: exact illustrated formats above are no longer mandated verbatim - just needs to be a clear MRP figure in Indian currency (₹/Rs.), inclusive of all taxes

exceptions: Alcoholic beverages/spirituous liquor: State Excise Laws apply instead (unless silent, then these rules apply)
Not required on domestic LPG cylinders under Administrative Price Mechanism

INSERTED by GSR 858(E), 07.09.2016: if the retail sale price of an essential commodity is fixed and notified by the Competent Authority under the Essential Commodities Act 1955, that government-fixed price applies instead of manufacturer-declared MRP CLARIFIED by departmental letter I-10/17/2023-W&M, dated 10.07.2023: names NPPA (National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority) as an example 'Competent Authority' for this override, and confirms that if a price revision is permitted by Government/NPPA/any other Statutory Body via their own notification, industry may revise MRP accordingly without violating this rule.

declarations.requirement: Where size of commodity is relevant, dimensions of the commodity; if different pieces have different dimensions, dimensions of each
Name, address, telephone number, email address of the person who can be, or the office which can be, contacted for consumer complaints
declarations.amendment_note: SUBSTITUTED by GSR 385(E), 14.05.2015, effective 01.01.2016 - substantively same content, restated wording (specifies contactable person/office rather than general contact details)

declarations.requirement: Stickers not permitted for altering/making required declarations, EXCEPT a sticker may be used to reduce MRP (must show revised lower MRP inclusive of all taxes, must not cover original MRP declaration)

Where commodity has multiple components packed in 2+ units sold as single commodity, declarations must appear on main package (which also carries info about accompanying packages), OR declarations on individual packages with intimation on main package. If sold as spare parts, all declarations on each package.
Every package containing genetically modified food shall bear the words 'GM' at the top of its Principal Display Panel
declarations.mandatory: conditional - applies only to GM food products

declarations.requirement: Every package containing soap, shampoo, toothpaste, and other cosmetics/toiletries shall bear at the top of its Principal Display Panel a RED (or brown) dot for products of non-vegetarian origin, or a GREEN dot for products of vegetarian origin
declarations.category_relevance: Category 4 (General Retail) checklist addition - directly checkable via image analysis (detect red/brown vs green dot on PDP)

declarations.requirement: It is permissible to affix a label on imported packages for making the declarations required under these rules (i.e., a sticker/label is an acceptable method for imported goods to meet declaration requirements, not just original printing)
declarations.category_relevance: Relevant to Country of Origin / imported product checks - confirms labels (not just original packaging print) are valid compliance method for imports

declarations.requirement: Nothing in this rule prevents a manufacturer/packer/importer from ALSO declaring (in addition to mandatory declarations): (a) Barcode, GTIN, or QR Code; (b) 'e-code' for net quantity assurance and other declarations, obtained as specified by Central Government; (c) logos of Government schemes (e.g., Swachh Bharat Mission), where authorised by Central Government
declarations.category_relevance: Relevant to barcode/QR/GTIN cross-verification feature - confirms these are legally recognized voluntary declarations, not something to flag as 'extra/unusual' content on a label

declarations.requirement: An E-Commerce entity shall ensure that the mandatory declarations under Rule 6(1) - EXCEPT the month and year of manufacture/packing - are displayed on the digital/electronic network used for e-commerce transactions

marketplace_safe_harbor.condition: For marketplace-model e-commerce, responsibility for correctness of declarations lies with the manufacturer/seller/dealer/importer (NOT the platform) IF the entity: (a) merely provides access to a communication system without controlling the info, (b) does not initiate transmission, select the receiver, or modify the info, (c) observes due diligence as an intermediary under the IT Act 2000 and other prescribed guidelines
marketplace_safe_harbor.loss_of_protection: Safe harbor does NOT apply if the entity: (a) conspired/abetted/aided/induced the unlawful act, or (b) upon actual knowledge or government notification of unlawful content, fails to expeditiously remove/disable access to it
marketplace_safe_harbor.clarification: This safe harbor provision does NOT exempt the physical pre-packaged commodity itself from bearing full declarations when delivered to the consumer - it only addresses platform liability for the DIGITAL listing

declarations.category_relevance: DIRECTLY relevant to your PS scope ('product listings') and your Digital-vs-Physical Listing Mismatch feature - this is the core legal basis for that entire feature

related_rule_6_10A.requirement: SUBSTITUTED by GSR 312(E), 27.04.2026: Every e-commerce entity OFFERING FOR SALE any imported product shall, with effect from 1st July 2027, ensure that the PRODUCT LISTING ITSELF contains a searchable and sortable filter specifying the country of origin
related_rule_6_10A.note: DIFFERENT KIND of requirement from the rest of Rule 6(10) - this is not about what's declared ON a listing/label, but about the e-commerce PLATFORM's UI/filtering functionality itself (a searchable/sortable country-of-origin filter across imported product listings)
related_rule_6_10A.checklist_relevance: This is a platform-level feature check, not a per-product label/listing check - relevant if your system audits e-commerce platform compliance as a whole (e.g., checking whether a marketplace's search UI offers this filter) rather than just scanning individual product listings. Different tooling/approach needed (UI/DOM inspection of the platform's search page) vs. your per-listing OCR/text-matching approach for other Rule 6(10) declarations.

amendment_history.gsr_128E_original: Original wording (GSR 128(E), 13.02.2026): 'shall provide the product listings... in a searchable and sortable filter' - effective 01.07.2026
amendment_history.gsr_312E_substitution: SUBSTITUTED by GSR 312(E), 27.04.2026: rewords to 'offering for sale' (broader than 'selling') and 'listing contains' (vs. platform 'provides'); MOST IMPORTANTLY pushes the effective date back a FULL YEAR, from 01.07.2026 to 01.07.2027

related_rule_6_10A.CRITICAL_STATUS_NOTE: As of today's date (Sept 2026), this requirement is NOT YET IN EFFECT - it was previously understood to be in effect from 01.07.2026 (per GSR 128(E)), but GSR 312(E) delayed it to 01.07.2027. Do not treat this as a currently-enforceable check until that date arrives.

declarations.requirement: SUBSTITUTED by GSR 226(E), 28.03.2022, effective 01.10.2022. Unit sale price in rupees, rounded to nearest TWO decimal places, declared as: (i) per gram if net quantity <1kg, per kilogram if >1kg; (ii) per centimetre if net length <1 metre, per metre if >1 metre; (iii) per millilitre if net volume <1 litre, per litre if >1 litre; (iv) per number or unit if sold by number/unit
declarations.category_relevance: Directly checkable format rule across all 3 categories - verify unit price uses the correct unit (g vs kg, cm vs m, ml vs L) based on the declared net quantity threshold
provisos: Alcoholic beverages/spirituous liquor: State Excise Laws (of the manufacturing state) apply instead
Unit sale price declaration NOT required if retail sale price (MRP) equals the unit sale price (i.e., no separate unit-price line needed for single-unit-equals-package items)

THIRD proviso INSERTED by GSR 722(E), 06.10.2023: unit sale price declaration is NOT required for a combination package, group package, or multi-piece package (as newly defined in Rule 2(ka)/(kb)/(kc)) - under these rules or any other law

amendment_history.gsr_779E_2021: Original version inserted, effective 01.04.2022 (later pushed to 01.10.2022) - simple per-unit format, no rounding rule or provisos
amendment_history.gsr_226E_2022: SUBSTITUTED just months later - added 2-decimal rounding rule, alcoholic beverage carve-out, and the 'MRP=unit price' exemption from declaring unit price separately

rule5_additional_subrules.critical_flag: CONFIRMED (was flagged as needing verification, now CONFIRMED via GSR 226(E)): Rule 5 was omitted by GSR 779(E) (eff. 01.10.2022, date corrected by GSR 226(E)), AND the Second Schedule ITSELF was separately and explicitly omitted by GSR 226(E) (clause 5), same effective date. historical_content_before_01_04_2022.note: Rule 5 renumbered as Rule 5(1) by GSR 427(E) in 2012; sub-rules (2) and (3) inserted then. ALL of the following ceased to have legal force from 01.04.2022:

sub_rules.requirement: When packages intended for retail sale are grouped together for sale as a retail package on promotional offer, every individual package within that group must still comply with Rule 6 declarations
sub_rules.successor: This exact requirement was RE-INSERTED elsewhere by GSR 779(E) as the new Rule 4(2) - see rule4_provisions section - so the substance survives, just relocated from Rule 5 to Rule 4

sub_rules.requirement: Notwithstanding the Second Schedule, manufacturers/importers may sell 'value based packages' at Rs.1-Rs.10 without matching Second Schedule standard quantities, provided all other Rule 6 declarations are made
sub_rules.note: No successor found yet - since Rule 5 (which this was an exception TO) is itself gone, this specific value-pack exception may now be moot/redundant rather than needing a replacement

sub_rules.requirement: If the Competent Authority under the Essential Commodities Act 1955 fixes/notifies standard quantity for an essential commodity, that overrides the Second Schedule
sub_rules.note: Also moot if Rule 5 itself is gone - no Second Schedule enforcement rule left to override

rule4_provisions.amendment_note: Original Rule 4 (enabling clause: 'No person shall pre-pack any commodity for sale unless declarations made') RENUMBERED as Rule 4(1) by GSR 779(E), 02.11.2021, effective 01.04.2022. New Rule 4(2) INSERTED at the same time.

sub_rules.requirement: No person shall pre-pack any commodity for sale unless the package has declarations as required under these rules (original Rule 4 text, now sub-rule 1)
When one or more packages intended for retail sale are grouped together for being sold as a retail package on promotional offer, every package of the group shall comply with provisions of Rule 6
sub_rules.note: This is substantively identical to the old Rule 5(2) promotional-grouping requirement - the provision was relocated here after Rule 5 was omitted, not newly invented

sub_rules.source_rule: Rule 4, Explanation-2 (original Explanation renumbered as Explanation-1)
sub_rules.requirement: Importers are allowed to make mandatory declarations AT BONDED WAREHOUSES of Authorised Economic Operator (AEO) Tier-2 and Tier-3 certified operators in India
sub_rules.proviso: Retail packages MUST have ALL mandatory declarations completed BEFORE LEAVING the bonded warehouse of the AEO Tier-2/Tier-3 certified operator
sub_rules.context_note: AEO Tier-2/Tier-3 are certifications administered by the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) to speed up customs clearance for compliant importers/exporters
sub_rules.checklist_relevance: Clarifies WHERE imported-product declarations may legally be completed (at a certified bonded warehouse) - relevant context for import-supply-chain compliance, though not directly verifiable from a single product image alone (more of a supply-chain/audit-trail fact than an OCR-checkable field)

font_size_rules.title: Principal display panel - its area, size and letter etc.
font_size_rules.major_overhaul_note: Rule 7 sub-rules (2), (3), (4), (5) and Table-I were ALL SUBSTITUTED, and Table-II was OMITTED ENTIRELY, by GSR 629(E), 23.06.2017, effective 01.01.2018. The structure below reflects the CURRENT law - the old separate Table-I (weight/volume) + Table-II (length/area/number) system is GONE, replaced by ONE unified area-based table.
font_size_rules.sub_rule_1: For packages with capacity <=10 cubic cm, PDP may be a card/tape affixed firmly to the package bearing required information (threshold raised from 5 to 10 cubic cm by GSR 385(E), 14.05.2015; reconfirmed explicitly in Rule 10 by GSR 629(E) too)
font_size_rules.sub_rule_2: SUBSTITUTED by GSR 629(E), effective 01.01.2018: The height of any numeral AND letter in the declaration shall be as per Table-I (single table now - no more separate weight/volume vs length/area/number tables) FURTHER PROVISO inserted by GSR 778(E), 23.10.2025: for packages containing MEDICAL DEVICES, the Medical Devices Rules 2017 apply for numeral/letter HEIGHT instead of Table-I - LM(PC) Table-I does not govern medical device font-size.
font_size_rules.sub_rule_3: SUBSTITUTED by GSR 629(E), effective 01.01.2018: width of letter/numeral not less than one-third of its height, except numeral '1' and letters (i), (I), (l) - substance same as before, wording restated FURTHER PROVISO inserted by GSR 778(E), 23.10.2025: for packages containing MEDICAL DEVICES, the Medical Devices Rules 2017 apply for numeral/letter WIDTH instead - same carve-out as height.

table_1_CURRENT.title: Table-I (CURRENT, replacing old Table-I AND Table-II combined) - Minimum height of numerals and letters, by Principal Display Panel Area

rows.correction_note: CORRECTED from 1.5 to 2.0 by corrigendum GSR 1373(E), dated 07.11.2017 - the original GSR 629(E) notification had a printing error here

table_2_OLD_HISTORICAL.status: OMITTED entirely by GSR 629(E), 23.06.2017, effective 01.01.2018 - no longer part of current law
table_2_OLD_HISTORICAL.historical_title: Old Table-II (pre-2018) - Minimum height of numeral - Net quantity in length/area/number
table_2_OLD_HISTORICAL.note: Kept here for historical reference only - use table_1_CURRENT above for all lookups going forward

table_1_OLD_HISTORICAL.status: SUPERSEDED by GSR 629(E) - the pre-2018 Table-I was structured around weight/volume tiers (200g/500g breakpoints), unlike the current area-based Table-I

sub_rule_4_pdp_area_calculation.note: This is the PDP area-calculation methodology, renumbered from sub-rule (5) to sub-rule (4) by GSR 629(E) - substance is the SAME formula originally inserted by GSR 385(E), just repositioned
sub_rule_4_pdp_area_calculation.title: Methodology for calculating Principal Display Panel (PDP) area
sub_rule_4_pdp_area_calculation.exclusions: Area calculation EXCLUDES: top, bottom, flange at top/bottom of cans, and shoulders/neck of bottles and jars

formulas.package_shape: Rectangular package (one side clearly the PDP)
formulas.formula: height x width of that side
40% of total surface area, OR the area considered to be the PDP

sub_rule_4_pdp_area_calculation.engineering_relevance: CRITICAL for your image-processing engine - this is the exact methodology to compute PDP area from a scanned/photographed package, now used to look up the SINGLE current Table-I above. For cylindrical packages (most common: bottles, cans, tubes) measure height and circumference (or diameter x pi), multiply, take 40%.

sub_rule_5_exemption_NARROWED.note: SUBSTITUTED by GSR 629(E), effective 01.01.2018 - this NARROWS the old blanket 'other law' exemption
sub_rule_5_exemption_NARROWED.general_rule: Rules 7(1)-(4) do not apply if the same info is already required to be given under any other law in force
sub_rule_5_exemption_NARROWED.critical_carveout: EXCEPT for: net weight, retail sale price (MRP), date of expiry/best-before/use-by date, and consumer care details - the font-size rules for THESE SPECIFIC FIELDS always apply regardless of any other law's exemption
sub_rule_5_exemption_NARROWED.checklist_relevance: Even if a product is governed by another law (e.g., Drugs Rules, Cosmetics Rules) that might otherwise exempt it from LM(PC) font-size rules, these 4 fields (net weight, MRP, expiry date, consumer care) must STILL meet Table-I font-size minimums

medical_devices_carveout.note: CONFIRMS medical devices are fully carved out of LM(PC) Rules for PDP definition (Rule 2(h)) and font-size rules (Rule 7(2)-(3)) - governed instead by the Medical Devices Rules 2017. This formalizes what was earlier only informally discussed/anticipated for your Category 2 scoping decision - medical devices should NOT be built into your Category 1/3/4 checklist engine; they fall under a separate regulatory framework (CDSCO/Medical Devices Rules 2017), consistent with your original scoping decision to exclude a full Category 2.

declaration_placement.requirement: Every declaration must appear on Principal Display Panel. Area surrounding quantity declaration must be free from printed information: (a) above/below by space >= height of numeral, (b) left/right by space >= twice height of numeral.

requirements: MRP and net quantity numerals printed/painted/inscribed in a colour that contrasts conspicuously with label background (9(1)(b))
Exception: blown/formed/molded info on glass/plastic need not be contrasting colour
Exception: handwritten/hand-script declarations must be clear, unambiguous, legible
No declaration may require reading through liquid commodity (9(2))
Outer container/wrapper must also carry all required declarations (9(3))
Rule 9(3) proviso OMITTED by GSR 385(E), 14.05.2015 - exact original proviso text not available from source document

NEW proviso INSERTED by GSR 629(E), 23.06.2017, effective 01.01.2018: no declaration is required on the INNER package if the OUTER package already contains ALL declarations required under these rules - i.e., inner packages can be declaration-free if the outer wrapper is fully compliant

quantity_declaration_rules.title: Declaration of name and address of manufacturer
quantity_declaration_rules.requirement: Conspicuous display of name+complete address of manufacturer (or manufacturer+packer if different; or importer if imported)
quantity_declaration_rules.small_package_exception: For packages <=10 cubic cm capacity (explicitly confirmed/reconfirmed as '10 cubic cm' by GSR 629(E), 23.06.2017, effective 01.01.2018 - closes earlier inconsistency where R7/R12 said 10cc but R10 hadn't been explicitly updated), a mark/inscription enabling consumer identification is sufficient
quantity_declaration_rules.foreign_made_local_pack: If commodity manufactured outside India but packed in India, PDP must also show name+address of Indian packer/importer
quantity_declaration_rules.complete_address_definition: FURTHER AMENDED by GSR 629(E), 23.06.2017, effective 01.01.2018 (Explanation renumbered as 'Explanation 1'): postal address at which the factory is situated OR company/firm is registered (BROADENED again - GSR 385(E) had narrowed this to registered-address-only in 2016; GSR 629(E) now allows EITHER factory location OR registered address); or street name + premises number + city/state + PIN code
quantity_declaration_rules.name_requirement: Must be actual corporate name, or trading name if unincorporated

complete_address_amendment_history.change: broadened to 'factory situated OR company/firm registered' (either now acceptable)

quantity_declaration_rules.title: General provisions relating to declaration of quantity
points: Net quantity excludes weight of wrappers/packaging materials
If commodity quantity doesn't vary with environment: declared qty = actual received qty, no 'when packed' qualifier allowed
If variation is negligible: declare qty accounting for variation so consumer gets >= declared quantity, still no 'when packed' qualifier
If variation is significant (per Third Schedule list): 'when packed' qualifier IS permitted

quantity_declaration_rules.title: Manner of quantity declaration
points: Unit must give accurate/adequate info: mass (solid/semi-solid/viscous), length (linear sale), area, volume (liquid/cubic), or number (count-sale) - except Fourth Schedule commodities
If declared by mass, manufacturer MAY optionally also declare item count
If weight/measure/number alone is insufficient, must also declare dimensions/number as needed
Additional consumer-relevant info must appear on same panel as other required declarations

PROHIBITED words that create exaggerated/misleading/inadequate impression: 'minimum', 'not less than', 'average', 'about', 'approximately' or similar. AMENDED by GSR 784(E), 24.10.2011 (eff. 01.07.2012): broadened to 'any word or expression of any sort whatsoever' - not limited to the listed examples, any term creating a misleading impression is prohibited

For packages <=10 cubic cm (reconfirmed by GSR 629(E), 23.06.2017, effective 01.01.2018): quantity declared on a tag/card/tape affixed such that it cannot be removed without opening container; must also carry manufacturer/packer identification
quantity_declaration_rules.checklist_relevance: The prohibited-words rule (point 5 above) is a directly checkable NLP/text-matching rule for your compliance engine - flag any label containing these terms near quantity declarations

quantity_declaration_rules.title: Statement of units of weight, measure or number
quantity_declaration_rules.prohibited: No 'dozen', 'score', 'gross', 'great gross' or similar count-words permitted on any package
quantity_declaration_rules.system: Only International System of Units (SI) permitted for net quantity
quantity_declaration_rules.number_symbol: SUBSTITUTED by GSR 779(E), 02.11.2021, effective 01.04.2022 (Rule 13(5)(ii)): for items sold by number, the word 'number', 'unit', 'piece', 'pair', 'set', or such other word representing the quantity shall be mentioned. CHANGE: previously required a fixed symbol ('N' or 'U'); now requires a descriptive WORD instead of a symbol
quantity_declaration_rules.litre_symbol_clarification: INSERTED by GSR 385(E), 14.05.2015 as Explanation to Rule 13(5): capital letter 'L' may be used for litre to avoid confusion with lowercase 'l' (letter I) and figure '1'
quantity_declaration_rules.checklist_relevance: Directly checkable: unit must be SI-compliant; flag if 'dozen'/'gross'/'score' appears; litre symbol 'L' (capital) is acceptable; for count-based items, look for descriptive words (number/unit/piece/pair/set) rather than the old N/U symbol convention

quantity_declaration_rules.title: Supplementary quantity declaration for multi-pack prepackages
quantity_declaration_rules.requirement: Where a prepackage contains multiple packages of the same commodity, the number of packages AND the quantity of each individual package must be indicated as a supplementary declaration
quantity_declaration_rules.example: If net quantity of each individual package is 10 grams and there are 10 such packages, the label must show '10 number x 10 gram' (number of packages multiplied by individual weight)
quantity_declaration_rules.category_relevance: Relevant to Category 1/4 multi-pack products (e.g., biscuit multipacks, snack combo packs) - directly checkable format: 'N number x Q unit'

quantity_declaration_rules.title: Dimensions for specific commodities
quantity_declaration_rules.applies_to: Bed-sheets, hemmed fabric materials, dhoties, sarees, napkins, pillow-covers, towels, table cloths, similar commodities
quantity_declaration_rules.requirement: Number and finished-size dimensions must be declared on package/label
quantity_declaration_rules.multi_piece_proviso: If package contains pieces of different dimensions, must declare dimensions AND retail sale price of EACH piece; dimensions+price must also be marked on each individual piece
quantity_declaration_rules.category_relevance: Directly relevant to Category 3 (Apparel/Textiles) checklist - saree/bedsheet/towel dimension+price-per-piece rule

quantity_declaration_rules.source: Rule 26(f) - CODIFIED BY LAW via GSR 648(E), 22.08.2022, effective 01.01.2023 (voluntary early adoption permitted immediately per the notification's own text). Department of Consumer Affairs advisory letters (2016-2017, referenced separately below) were the INFORMAL PRECURSOR to this now-formal rule.
quantity_declaration_rules.source_type: Formal Rule 26(f) exemption clause (legally binding) - UPGRADED from the earlier informal advisory-letter guidance
quantity_declaration_rules.title: Loose vs Pre-packaged Garment/Hosiery Labeling Requirements (NOW A FORMAL RULE 26(f) EXEMPTION)
quantity_declaration_rules.core_principle: Rule 26(f) formally EXEMPTS garments/hosiery sold loose or open (where the consumer can inspect before buying) from the full Chapter II declarations, SUBJECT TO a reduced, legally mandated 4-point declaration set (see current_legal_checklist below). This supersedes the earlier informal advisory letters, which addressed the same practical question but without the force of a codified Rule.
quantity_declaration_rules.pre_packaged_test: A garment that the consumer sees for style/design, tries on for fit, and touches/feels the fabric before purchase, and is then delivered to the consumer, is NOT a pre-packaged commodity (i.e., in-store try-on garments = loose, not pre-packaged)

loose_garment_checklist.note: LIMITED declaration set - NOT the full Rule 6 checklist

required_fields.requirement: Internationally recognizable size indicator (S/M/L/XL etc.) ALONG WITH metric notation in cm or m. 'TO FIT SIZE' may be used instead of just 'Size', at trade's convenience
Name, full address, and Customer Care number of the manufacturer

pre_packaged_garment_checklist.note: FULL Rule 6 declarations apply (see R6_1_a through R6_11, R14) for garments that ARE pre-packaged (not loose/open-for-inspection) - this is the standard checklist, not a reduced one
pre_packaged_garment_checklist.size_declaration_rule: Metric units (cm or m) are the PRIMARY/required size declaration (per Rule 14); S/M/L/XL etc. may be shown as ADDITIONAL information only, not as a substitute for metric dimensions

quantity_declaration_rules.checklist_relevance: CRITICAL for Category 3 architecture - confirms the two-tier checklist structure: (1) Pre-check whether garment is loose/open-for-inspection (finished product) or pre-packaged, (2) Route to the appropriate checklist - loose garments get the LEGALLY-BINDING 4-field check above (Rule 26(f)), pre-packaged garments get the full Rule 6 checklist with metric-primary sizing. If sold online, both categories also trigger the e-commerce display requirement.

current_legal_checklist.early_adoption: Manufacturers/packers/importers may declare this information with IMMEDIATE EFFECT even before the formal 01.01.2023 commencement date (per the notification's final proviso)
current_legal_checklist.applies_to: Finished products ONLY (per proviso - raw/unfinished textile goods are not covered by this exemption)

required_fields.requirement: Of the manufacturer, OR marketer, OR brand owner, OR importer (any one) - PLUS country of origin/manufacture if the product is imported
BOTH an email ID AND a phone number required (stricter than the earlier advisory, which only generically required a 'customer care no.')

SUBSTITUTED by GSR 722(E), 06.10.2023 (item iii): size may be declared EITHER as metric notation (cm or m) ALONE, OR as internationally recognizable size indicators (S/M/L/XL/XXL/XXXL) ALONG WITH metric notation - metric-only is now sufficient by itself; letter-size is an optional addition, not mandatory alongside metric (loosened from the original GSR 648(E) wording which required both together)
Maximum retail price inclusive of all taxes, in Indian currency

current_legal_checklist.ecommerce_requirement: If such a loose garment/hosiery product is sold via e-commerce, the SAME information must ALSO be displayed on the e-commerce website - directly ties to Rule 6(10)'s e-commerce declaration requirement and your listing-mismatch feature

historical_advisory_precursor.note: The Department of Consumer Affairs issued 2 advisory/clarification letters in 2016-2017 addressing this same loose-vs-pre-packaged question BEFORE it was formally codified as Rule 26(f). Key concepts carried forward into the formal rule:
historical_advisory_precursor.pre_packaged_test: A garment that the consumer sees for style/design, tries on for fit, and touches/feels the fabric before purchase, and is then delivered to the consumer, is NOT a pre-packaged commodity (i.e., in-store try-on garments = loose, not pre-packaged) - this practical test remains a useful interpretive guide even though Rule 26(f) itself doesn't repeat this exact wording
historical_advisory_precursor.wording_flexibility: 'TO FIT SIZE' may be used instead of just 'Size', per the original advisory - not explicitly repeated in Rule 26(f) but not contradicted either

quantity_declaration_rules.title: Dimensions/weight where linked to price
quantity_declaration_rules.requirement: Where dimensions and/or weight has a relationship to the commodity's price, the quantity declaration must also include that dimension/weight/combination

quantity_declaration_rules.title: Number of usable sheets
quantity_declaration_rules.applies_to: Aluminum foil, facial tissues, waxed paper, toilet paper, or similar sheet-type commodities
quantity_declaration_rules.requirement: Must declare number of usable sheets AND dimensions of each sheet

quantity_declaration_rules.title: Dimensions for container-type commodities
quantity_declaration_rules.applies_to: Bags, boxes, cups, pans or similar items sold as containers for other materials
requirements: Bag-type: number of bags + linear dimensions (whether in perforated roll or otherwise)
Square/oblong/rectangular containers: number of containers + length, width, and depth if required
Circular/round containers (not cups): number + diameter, and depth if necessary
If container's holding capacity is referenced via standard weight/measure on label, that reference must be included in the quantity declaration

third_schedule_when_packed_qualifier.title: Declaration of quantity (sold by weight or volume) which may be qualified by the words 'When packed'
third_schedule_when_packed_qualifier.note: Commodities in this list are permitted to use the 'When packed' qualifier per Rule 11(4), since their weight/volume may vary significantly due to environmental conditions

part_1_weight_volume.title: Maximum permissible errors on net quantities declared by weight or by volume
part_1_weight_volume.rounding_rule: Percentage-based error rounded to nearest one-tenth of g/ml for quantities <=1000 g/ml; rounded to next whole g/ml for quantities above 1000 g/ml

part_2_length_area_number.title: Maximum permissible errors on net quantities declared by length, area or number
part_2_length_area_number.applies_to: Commodities not specified in the First Schedule (Part 1)

rows.max_error: 2% of declared quantity up to 10 metre, thereafter 1% of declared quantity
4% of declared quantity up to 10 sq. metre, thereafter 1% of declared quantity

sub_rules.requirement: A wholesale dealer shall be allowed to sell pre-packaged commodities directly to industrial and institutional consumers
sub_rules.note: Confirms wholesale dealers (not just manufacturers/importers) can be a valid source for institutional/industrial consumer packages - relevant to the definitions.institutional_consumer / industrial_consumer sourcing requirement

sub_rules.requirement: Unless otherwise specifically provided under any other law, no manufacturer/packer/importer shall declare DIFFERENT maximum retail prices on an IDENTICAL pre-packaged commodity by adopting restrictive or unfair trade practices (as defined under the Consumer Protection Act)
